I do not know how long we spent on that floor and then later there is transportation pallets were brought in and several of them were brought in. Some people were able to sit down. Maybe a few people were able to lie down to rest a little bit, and the rest would go on standing and then people were taking turns.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Were there toilet facilities in the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the hangar itself, there was no toilet. The toilet that was used at first was in another building. Later a latrine was made outside of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage may we go into private session, your Honours, for the reason that this witness would divulge details which may reveal the identity of the witness. For that reason I ask your Honours to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: We are going to have a private session now. You can continue, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: We can continue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall your release from prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the release, we were taken by Ante Cakic to cut grass. I think it was his property, I am not sure. He told us that there would be an exchange. We at first did not believe it because we missed several of them -- we had missed several of them before. Then when we were taken back to the camp I was sort of dozing off. I only heard some shouts, in fact it was some people were being called out and somebody said: "Whoever I call out should step outside" and all the cells were already unlocked. My name was called out, I stepped outside and the saw that the International Red Cross representatives were there and the interpreter said that we were going to be exchanged. I noted when we were about to leave, Dzemo came over and told us, we were about five or six, myself included, he told us to pass a message on around Zenica that Dzemo was the biggest Ustasha of them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, together with you, do you know how many other people were released with you that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were not many of us. Some people were released into some kind of a house arrest in Skradno. Some were ill. Some had been exchanged before, so we were not many, maybe 30. I do not know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you know the date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean do I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you know the date on which you were released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 19th June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: After your release, where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just wanted to add that before this, some people stayed behind in the camp, like the man from Syria called Mohamed. Myself and the other detainees were transferred to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Now, after you were released, did you have occasion to see a doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were brought to Zenica, the medical care was already provided, so a physician saw me as soon as I got off the bus and he asked me whether I had any complaints. Of course, I knew I did, but I wanted to see my parents and the rest of my family, even though I was not sure where all of them were. Later my brother came and found me there. He had heard that an exchange was going to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Did you suffer as a result of those beatings whilst in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have -- I suffer certain consequences, mostly my back and my two teeth were broken and you may have noticed that here I -- my teeth, some already were damaged before, but in the camp I got further damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I have no further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, I should like to know whether you have questions to put to the witness and, if so, how much time do you think you need, as it is almost 5.30 now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence has a number of questions to ask of this witness, so we would suggest that we close for the day and that we be allowed to ask our questions tomorrow, in continuity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mikulicic. We are going to adjourn for today, therefore. We meet again here tomorrow. Thank you for today. Until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: on Tuesday, 3rd March 1998)
